subject: Discovery recap — reliability & graceful degradation (FinServ)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Kim <claire.kim@finserv.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — reliability & graceful degradation (FinServ)

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the candid run-through of the reliability issues you
re seeing in production. Quick recap from our side (please correct me where I missed something):

Pain points you called out:
- Recent regional platform incident causing ~30m customer-facing degradation (retries/timeouts surfaced to end users).
- Inconsistent latency from your current LLM vendor during peak windows (p95 increases 4x).
- No consistent fallback strategy: when the primary model/region is unhealthy, some traffic just times out rather than failing gracefully.
- Cost unpredictability when retry storms increase token usage.

Current stack you described:
- Hybrid architecture: primary calls to a third-party hosted LLM (multi-tenant), on-prem inference for sensitive workloads, Redis-based prefix cache for repeated queries.
- Control plane in AWS us-east with a passive failover to an on-prem cluster for certain flows.

Success criteria (what would make this a successful project):
- No visible customer errors during regional incidents (graceful degradation / fallback) — target: <1% user-facing errors in incident windows.
- Predictable latency under load (p95 target <= 500ms for critical flows).
- Clear SLOs and an SLA we can agree on (availability target + incident MTTR expectations).
- Cost predictability: we should be able to forecast incremental token spend during normal and degraded modes.

Incident history you shared:
- Jan 15, 2026: multi-zone latency spike affecting 10-15% of requests for ~45 minutes; retries amplified load and increased cost (postmortem attached).
- Oct 2, 2025: regional provider outage; some traffic failed over to on-prem but throttling caused elevated error rates for 30 minutes.

Redwood's initial recommendations we discussed:
- Automated graceful degradation policies: route to smaller/cheaper model variants with the same safety filters when latency/backpressure thresholds hit.
- Region-aware routing + hot standby regions: automatic reroute to a healthy region with automatic KV cache warming to reduce cold-start errors.
- Dedicated/reserved capacity option for critical workloads to ensure predictable throughput during spikes.
- Prefix/KV caching and request-level fallbacks to limit burst token cost during retries.
- Clear SLO/SLA templates we can adapt to FinServ's compliance needs.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Share our SOC 2 summary and a draft SLA template (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep dive with our infra lead (Rafael) and your platform engineers — target Mar 9-11.
3) Demo dedicated capacity + failover flow (short recording + Q&A).
4) Provide a preliminary cost delta for moving critical flows to reserved capacity + fallback policies.

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf, SLA_template.docx

If that all looks right, I'll (a) share the attachments now, (b) book the deep dive for next week, and (c) prepare a short sample runbook showing the fallback logic.

Thanks — Jonas

Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

>

>

>

From: Claire Kim <claire.kim@finserv.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@finserv.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — reliability & graceful degradation (FinServ)

Jonas — thanks for the thorough recap. Everything captures the discussion well. A few follow-ups from our side:

- Please include an explicit fallback path to a smaller model (we use a distilled model internally) with identical safety/sanitization steps. Evan wants to validate that safety filters are preserved during fallback.
- Can you indicate expected RPO/RTO targets you can commit to for the dedicated offering? Evan will need numbers to take to procurement (e.g., availability targets, MTTR ranges).
- I attached the Jan 15 incident postmortem (FinServ_incident_report.pdf) — it shows the retry amplification pattern we saw when our primary model slowed.

We are available next week for the technical deep dive but prefer mornings PST. Thanks for sharing the SOC2 summary and SLA template.

Claire Kim
Senior Platform PM, FinServ Corp
claire.kim@finserv.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Kim <claire.kim@finserv.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — reliability & graceful degradation (FinServ)

Claire — quick note from the infra side:

- For dedicated capacity we can offer 99.9% availability for reserved pools with an enterprise SLA (we'll share the exact SLA template and MTTR bands in the doc). For hard SLO commitments (99.95%+), we'd recommend a multi-region reserved setup plus active standby.
- Fallbacks to smaller model variants are supported and we preserve the same moderation/safety hooks; we can show a short run-through of the model-switch flow in the deep dive.
- I put together an internal playbook for graceful degradation and region failover (link below). We'll use that as a starting point and adapt to FinServ's constraints.

Proposed deep dive times (PST morning slots): Mar 9 9:00-10:00, Mar 10 9:30-10:30. Rafael will own infra + failover demo; Marissa will cover SLA/compliance mapping.

Link: https://redwood-internal/docs/dedicated-playbook.pdf

Rafael Mendes
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

I'll follow up with a short agenda for the deep dive later today. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Jonas
